_doc: MPC robot geometry/limits and MPC tuning, loaded via --robot-spec=<path>. Absent keys keep the compiled defaults (mpc::RobotSpec::defaults()/mpc::MpcParams::defaults()); unknown keys produce a stderr warning but do not fail loading. The MPC prediction horizon (mpc::kHorizon in include/mpc/MpcCore.h) is a compile-time constant and is intentionally NOT configurable here. DEADBAND FIELDS ARE HARDWARE PROPERTIES: min_moving_speed/min_sustain_speed describe this project's actual robots' real BLDC breakaway/sustain thresholds (m/s) and drive BOTH mpc_robot_sim's opt-in --deadband plant model (see MPC/include/mpc/SimCore.h; the sim also needs its own --deadband --min-moving-speed=/--min-sustain-speed= flags to actually enable it) AND mpc_controller's LAUNCH GOVERNOR (see MPC/include/mpc/LaunchGovernor.h, which activates automatically whenever min_moving_speed > 0). Compiled defaults are 0.0/0.0 -- an IDEAL, deadband-free plant with the governor inactive -- so passing --robot-spec=<this file> is what opts a controller INTO real-hardware behavior; simulated/test runs that want an ideal plant should omit --robot-spec (or override it away) rather than relying on any implicit zeroing. launch_margin (headroom the launch governor commands above min_moving_speed when launching from rest) defaults to 0.1 regardless and is inert whenever min_moving_speed is 0. max_breakaway_accel (default 3.0, must be >= max_accel) is the accel ceiling mpc_robot_sim's --deadband plant allows a RECEIVED command while stalled (models ESC launch-current headroom); it has no effect once the plant is moving or while --deadband is off. settle_position_tolerance/settle_cooldown_s/settle_max_attempts (defaults 0.03m/1.0s/3) tune the LAUNCH GOVERNOR's CORRECTION-LAUNCH behavior (see LaunchGovernor.h): a bounded, rate-limited nudge that lets a robot finish closing a residual position error at an otherwise-stationary reference instead of parking short forever; inert whenever min_moving_speed<=0.
